Theme

Latin word

impediō

impediō, impedīre, impedīvī, impedītum

verb, fourth conjugation, transitive

entangle; make (a matter) hard to manage; hinder, get in the way

In this lexicon

  • complicate

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. And. 3.5.11: vidēn’ mē cōnsiliīs tuīs miserum impedītum esse? (Lewis & Short); Ter. And. 3.5.13: rem impedītam, “an intricate affair” (Lewis & Short)

  • prevent

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 60: nec aetās impedit, quōminus agrī colendī studia teneāmus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fat. 1: casus quīdam, nē facerem, impedīvit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 328; Traupman 404

Examples

  • vidēn’ mē cōnsiliīs tuīs miserum impedītum esse?

    don’t you see that your schemes have got poor me into a tangle?Ter. And. 3.5.11 (Lewis & Short)

  • dum aliōs servat, sē impedīvit interim

    while he was saving others, he got himself into a tanglePlaut. Rud. prol. 37 (Lewis & Short)
